answers.children: Yes — Lagotto Romagnolos are good with children when their energetic nature is channelled into play that matches the curly-coated truffle hunter’s stamina and intelligence. Their affectionate bond with family makes them attentive playmates yet their boundless drive can overwhelm smaller children during rough games drawn from their wetland retrieving past. The medium build allows safe interaction without the risk of accidental knocks common in heavier breeds. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — Lagotto Romagnolos generally get along with other pets when raised together thanks to their loyal family focus and intelligent sociability. Their history as water retrievers and later truffle hunters gives low prey drive around household animals yet they can show reserved caution toward unfamiliar dogs. Same-sex tension remains minimal provided early introductions respect their energetic boundaries.
answers.exercise: Lagotto Romagnolos need 60 to 90 minutes of vigorous daily exercise or they channel their high energy into destructive digging and chewing rooted in their truffle-hunting drive. Scent games that mimic locating underground delicacies suit the intelligent curly-coated breed best along with running swimming or long hikes that echo their original marsh retrieving work. Under-exercised dogs become restless and bark sharply at household sounds.
answers.shedding: No — Lagotto Romagnolos shed very little year-round because their medium curly coat lacks the dense undercoat of many sporting breeds. The tight curls trap dead hair inside the coat so minimal loose strands reach furniture or floors yet regular grooming prevents matting that occurs behind the ears and on the legs from their active wetland heritage.
answers.hypoallergenic: The Lagotto Romagnolo has a medium curly coat that sheds very little and produces minimal loose hair around the house. This dense, water-repellent texture traps dander rather than spreading it, which is why the breed is frequently suggested to allergy sufferers despite the fact that no breed is genuinely hypoallergenic.
answers.training: Yes — Lagotto Romagnolos are easy to train because their intelligence and eagerness to work with family stem directly from centuries of truffle hunting that demanded focus and quick learning. The affectionate temperament makes them responsive to positive methods while their energetic drive rewards tasks that engage the exceptional sense of smell developed for forest foraging.
answers.lifespan: Lagotto Romagnolos live 15 to 17 years. Their medium size and robust build from the Romagna wetlands support this longevity when the high energy is met through daily scent work or retrieving games that match their original purpose as water dogs turned truffle hunters.
answers.size: Lagotto Romagnolos reach 24-35 lb and stand 16-19 in at the shoulder. The compact muscular proportions give a sturdy feel in the home without the bulk of larger sporting breeds so the curly-coated Italian fits neatly on sofas yet still possesses the substance needed for hours of digging in forests.
answers.barking: Lagotto Romagnolos bark moderately and mainly to alert the household to anything unusual. Their reserved nature with strangers combines with the intelligent watchdog instinct developed during Renaissance marsh retrieving and later woodland truffle hunts so the sharp insistent bark warns rather than disturbs neighbours constantly.
answers.apartment: No — Lagotto Romagnolos do not suit apartment living well because their high energy and need for scent games lead to restlessness and destructive behaviour indoors. The intelligent truffle-hunting drive makes settling difficult without 60 to 90 minutes of daily activity that echoes their Italian wetland and forest heritage.
answers.first-time: No — Lagotto Romagnolos are not ideal as a first dog because their high energy demands structured daily exercise and mental tasks that prevent destructive chewing if the intelligent working drive goes unmet. Novices may struggle with the loyal yet clingy affection and reserved attitude toward strangers that require consistent guidance drawn from the breed’s specialised Italian hunting background.
